page: Amazon Web Services m7i.large is a general-purpose instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8488C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the Nitro hypervisor, has no local storage, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations, alongside cryptographic accelerations like AES and SHA_NI. In single-core benchmarks, the instance demonstrates average performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1747.0 and a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1845.29. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are lower, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2133.0 and a Passmark memory score of 864.32, reflecting the resource constraints of a 2-vCPU configuration.

Given its hardware profile, the m7i.large is positioned as an entry-level general-purpose instance. It is suited for workloads that require modern CPU instruction sets but do not demand high multi-core throughput or massive memory bandwidth, such as light web serving, basic text processing, and single-threaded utility tasks. The instance offers a cost-efficient entry point to the Intel Gen7 platform, though workloads requiring high-performance database operations or multi-threaded compilation may experience bottlenecks due to the single physical core limitation.
